claims.statement: Polish law gives owners of wind or solar resources that execute qualifying non-market redispatch instructions a compensation route; the connecting operator calculates and pays, subject to the EU-referenced rules.

Entitlement is narrower than installed OZE capacity: current law excludes non-firm connection arrangements, selection depends on controllability and size, and PSE limits claims to owners whose installations actually executed listed PSE-related instructions.

The general compensation claim expires 180 days after the last day of the month in which the instruction was executed; separately, auction-support information is due within 14 days and missing it can remove that support component.

Curtailment volume is material at sector level: in 2024 PSE ordered about 597.26 GWh of PV and 125.1 GWh of wind non-market reductions, while DSO-initiated reductions added 24.12 GWh PV and 2.8 GWh wind.

DSO-initiated 2024 curtailment was highly concentrated: only 3 of 188 DSOs used it, and Enea accounted for 98.8% of DSO PV and 85.7% of DSO wind reductions. National MWh therefore do not establish a broad reachable owner base.

URE reported 4,333 producers and 8,077 small OZE installations at year-end 2025, creating a broad prospecting universe for the 50 kW-1 MW segment, but it does not identify which owners executed compensable instructions or were underpaid.

PSE's free WOZE portal already provides installation registration, lists eligible PSE instructions, validates claim inputs, supports corrections, tracks status, delivers settlement information and accepts owner-authorized service providers.

PSE publishes the accepted PV and wind counterfactual methods. They use operator/owner meter data plus irradiation, wind-power curves, area forecasts or regression paths, and PSE publishes settlement prices and offers detailed calculations on request.

Asset-level workflow access is permissioned rather than openly reusable: WOZE roles require the owner's business-partner administrator and acceptance authority, while PSE's redispatch B2B API uses mTLS, business-partner registration and defines the participant as the owner, DSO or an authorized representative.

PSE does not state an end-to-end review SLA: review time depends on incoming volume and DSO data. It commits to payment within 21 days only after it receives the accounting document and accepted settlement information.

A direct Polish competitor already offers the same wedge: SCADA connection, 15-minute monitoring, deadline alerts, automated monthly claims and a separate law-firm route. Its posted pricing is EUR 119/month for one plant, EUR 699/month for up to five plants/20 MW and EUR 2,325/month enterprise, each plus a 5% law-firm success fee.

The direct competitor explicitly says its examples are hypothetical and that it will publish case studies once it has clients; therefore its presence proves offer saturation and a price anchor, not paid demand or successful incremental recoveries.

Existing asset managers can bundle the adjacent work: VSB advertises grid/feed-in management, documentation, data analysis, contract and claims management, receivables, settlements and PPA support for Polish wind and solar assets.

There is genuine calculation ambiguity: the European Commission says fair-payment calculation remains unclear, and the current UD284 proposal says existing rules are tailored to schedule-based sales and do not work the same way for pay-as-produced PPAs.

No located authoritative or merchant evidence quantifies how often reachable owners fail to claim, how often PSE under-calculates, or the cash added by a second-look service over WOZE, O&M and legal support. Avoided loss and aggregate curtailed MWh are not capturable revenue.

Outcome data do not automatically create a moat: official methods and system data are published, asset-specific access is owner-scoped, and cross-client reuse of telemetry, contracts and settlement outcomes would require explicit contractual rights and privacy/security controls.

At a test price of 3% of incremental cash, an assumed PLN 150,000 incremental recovery produces PLN 4,500 revenue. With assumed delivery cost of PLN 1,200 and a 15% referral share, contribution is PLN 2,625 (58%); recoveries below roughly PLN 160,000 do not reach 60% contribution margin under those assumptions.

A founder-net-worth path based only on a 3% incremental-recovery fee requires approximately 1,235 active owners at PLN 150,000 average incremental recovery per owner-year, 25% EBITDA margin, a 4x EBITDA value and 90% founder ownership to reach about PLN 5.0 million of founder equity; the eligible denominator and repeat rate needed for that scale are unproven.

contrary_evidence: The operator itself supplies a no-fee, increasingly automated claim portal with eligible-event lists, validation, corrections and status tracking. [evidence: SRC03]

PSE defines and publishes the counterfactual calculation paths and provides detailed calculations on request, limiting the proprietary value of merely reproducing the official formula. [evidence: SRC02, SRC04, SRC05]
An exact technology-plus-law-firm competitor is already live with public subscriptions and a 5% success-fee anchor. [evidence: SRC10]

Professional asset managers already sell grid, data, contract, receivables and claims management to the same owners, so a proposed channel can internalize the service or compete with it. [evidence: SRC11]

Non-firm connection terms remove entitlement, actual execution is required, and DSO curtailment is geographically/operator concentrated; installed capacity materially overstates eligible buyers. [evidence: SRC01, SRC02, SRC06]
The only exact competitor found discloses no client case studies, so there is still no observed paid behavior or proof that incremental recovery exceeds native settlement. [evidence: SRC10]
